$comment: The contract's method surface, mirrored from
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS: contract-corpus.json checks that every method on the
TurboModule spec has a fixture. That is spec -> corpus. Nothing checked
contract -> spec, so a method could be added to the contract and silently
never bridged, with a green gate.
That is not hypothetical. Autocapture was added to the contract and this
package shipped zero autocapture surface; the corpus gate passed anyway,
and an iOS reviewer caught it rather than CI.
Update this file in the same commit that adopts a contract change. It is
the local, machine-readable half of a document that lives in another repo.

methods.record: record(eventTitle, userId?, accountId?, data?, userAttributes?, accountAttributes?) -> Bool
methods.consent: consent(action, validUntil, email?, message?, category?) -> Bool

diagnostics.getSdkVersion: Bridged, but not a contract method. Reports the NATIVE SDK's version — intempt-swift or intempt-android — which is what someone debugging an integration needs and which no contract method exposes. Kept in its own category rather than notBridged, because it IS on the spec.

notBridged.isOptedIn: Pure JavaScript convenience over hasOptedOut(). Never crosses the bridge, so it has no native method and no fixture.
notBridged.doNotCaptureText: Android-only, takes a native View. No bridge representation and no cross-platform meaning. The contract's one sanctioned permanent exception.
notBridged.mainInstance: Resolved in the JavaScript instance registry; the native side is addressed by instanceName on every call.
